newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes $2 higher, Brent at $18.36.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes $2 higher, Brent at $18.36.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed $2.00 a tonne higher in low voume on Wednesday, reflecting stronger U.S. product markets, brokers said.
Front month August settled at $165.00 a tonne, 25 cents off the high, and September finished up $1.50 at $166.25 a tonne.
"It was a steady close, reflecting New York," one gas oil trader said.
Sept Brent was 14 cents up at $18.36 a barrel at 1655 GMT.
U.S. heating oil and gasoline were higher on slightly stronger stock and demand data from the American Petroleum Institute and the U.S. Department of Energy.
The API and DOE showed gasoline stocks dropping 2.8 million and 2.3 million barrels respctively, much steeper draws than traders had anticipated.
NYMEX gasoline was trading 0.78 cent firmer at 60.80 cents a gallon. Heating oil was up 0.60 cent at 53.30 cents a gallon.
IPE Gas oil's upside is limited by the high dollar which is curbing physical demand particularly into Germany.
NYMEX crude was helped by DOE data showing U.S. crude stocks fell 2.0 million barrels last week, compared with a rise of 1.42 million shown in API data late on Tuesday.
Both crude and gas oil were likely to continue to trade
in narrow ranges until there is further news on the resumption of Iraqi crude exports, brokers said.
A U.N. spokesman on Tuesday said the approval of Iraq's aid distribution plan, on which Iraq insists before it resumes exports, was not expected until the end of July.
